title_en: Steven Spielberg Will Direct a Western Written by Paul Thomas Anderson and Starring Cillian Murphy
summary_en: Steven Spielberg is going big with his next film, which is a Western written by Paul Thomas Anderson and starring Cillian Murphy.
body_en:
Steven Spielberg is going big with his next film, which is a Western written by Paul Thomas Anderson and starring Cillian Murphy.
Deadline confirmed that Spielberg is already developing his next film following the release of Disclosure Day this summer, and it'll be an adaptation of the 2024 novel The Heart in Winter. The book is set in 1891 amid a harsh winter in a Montana mining town. It follows a degenerate poet and ballad-maker who crosses paths with the new bride of the town's mine captain, sparking an intense love affair before they run west together with pursuers hot on their tail. Spielberg described the project to Deadline as a story about "people who refused to settle for a life that is less than they deserve but maybe more than they can handle."
Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley will play the leading characters in the film, which is apparently still untitled despite being sourced from an existing piece of work. He has also teamed with Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, who is penning the script. This marks the first time Anderson has fully written a script that he himself hasn't directed, but he has done uncredited punch-ups and rewrites on other movies like Killers of the Flower Moon.
“It’s really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team," said Spielberg about the partnership.
The two began flirting with the idea of working together back in January while Anderson was on the awards trail for One Battle After Another, which cleaned up at the various ceremonies and led to him receiving an Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay . Naturally, that kind of prestige makes him a smart pick to adapt a layered novel such as this one. The two binged old Westerns on 35mm film as part of their creative process.
Spielberg's untitled Western is currently targeting a 2028 release, with filming set to begin next winter. The 79-year-old director was also quick to note that this is not his final project and denied that this was some kind of metaphor about his career, where he gets to literally ride off into the sunset at the end.
“If I wanted to ride off into the sunset, I would have done Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade next, and I could have had those characters literally riding off into the sunset as the credits roll,” Spielberg said.
Photo by Presley Ann/Getty Images for Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
